facts.statement: A second specimen, IVPP 18406, consists of a skull, jaws, and the first three neck vertebrae.
facts.quote: A second specimen, IVPP 18406, has also been assigned to Ikrandraco; it consists of a skull and jaws and the first three neck vertebrae.

facts.statement: Both known specimens come from the Aptian-age Lower Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation of Liaoning, dated to approximately 120 million years ago.
facts.quote: Both specimens come from the Aptian-age Lower Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation of Liaoning, with an estimated date of 120 million years ago.

facts.statement: Ikrandraco was described in 2014 by Wang Xiaolin and colleagues but was not formally named according to ICZN rules until 2020.
facts.quote: It was described in 2014 by Wang Xiaolin and colleagues, but was not properly named according to ICZN rules until 2020.

facts.statement: The specific epithet machaerorhynchus means "sabre snout" in Greek.
facts.quote: The specific name means "sabre snout" in Greek.

facts.statement: The holotype of the related species Lonchodectes machaerorhynchus was found near Cambridge in the Cambridge Greensand, which dates to the Cenomanian but contains reworked fossils from the Albian.
facts.quote: Its holotype, CAMSM B54855, was found near Cambridge, in a layer of the Cambridge Greensand dating from the Cenomanian but containing reworked fossils from the Albian.

facts.statement: In 2013, Rodrigues and Kellner reassigned Lonchodectes machaerorhynchus and L. microdon to the genus Lonchodraco because they considered Lonchodectes to be a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: In 2013, paleontologists Taissa Rodrigues and Alexander Kellner made an extensive review of the species of Ornithocheirus, and stated that the generic name Lonchodectes would have been a nomen dubium, and therefore reassigned both Lonchodectes machaerorhynchus and L. microdon into the genus Lonchodraco, creating Lonchodraco machaerorhynchus and L. microdon.

facts.statement: Alexander Averianov reassigned Lonchodraco machaerorhynchus to Ikrandraco and declared Lonchodraco microdon a junior synonym of I. machaerorhynchus.
facts.quote: In his review of Lonchodectidae, Alexander Averianov reassigned Lonchodraco machaerorhynchus to Ikrandraco, and also declared Lonchodraco microdon (including O. oweni) a junior synonym of I. machaerorhynchus.

facts.statement: Ikrandraco is notable for an unusual skull featuring a crest on the lower jaw.
facts.quote: It is notable for its unusual skull, which features a crest on the lower jaw.

facts.statement: Ikrandraco has a very long, low skull where the height at the quadrates is less than 19% of the skull length, featuring a blade-like crest on the lower jaw but no crest on the upper jaw, a combination unseen in other pterosaurs.
facts.quote: Ikrandraco avatar is notable for having a very long, low skull (the height of the back of the skull, at the quadrates, is less than 19% the length of the skull), with a prominent blade-like crest on the underside of the lower jaw and no corresponding crest on the tip of the upper jaw, a crest combination not seen in other pterosaurs to date.

facts.statement: The posterior edge of the lower jaw crest has a hook-like process.
facts.quote: The posterior edge of the crest also has a hook-like process.

facts.statement: The genus name means "Ikran dragon", referencing the flying creatures from the movie Avatar that possess a crest on their jaw.
facts.quote: El nombre del género significa "dragón ikran", en referencia a las criaturas voladoras de la película Avatar, que poseen una cresta en su mandíbula.

facts.statement: The only described species is I. avatar, a second reference to the movie Avatar.
facts.quote: La especie tipo y única descrita es I. avatar, una segunda referencia a esta película.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the hook on the crest may have served as an attachment point for a throat pouch to store food, similar to a pelican.
facts.quote: The hook on the crest may have been an attachment point for a throat pouch for storing food, akin to a pelican.

facts.statement: Ikrandraco was a piscivore that lived alongside Liaoningopterus gui and Guidraco venator, but its smaller, less robust teeth suggest it occupied a different ecological niche.
facts.quote: Ikrandraco was an approximate contemporary of the distantly related anhanguerians Liaoningopterus gui and Guidraco venator, and all three are regarded as piscivores, but Ikrandraco differed from them in its much smaller and less robust teeth, indicating it had a different niche.

facts.statement: Analyses recovered Ikrandraco as a member of the family Lonchodraconidae and as the sister taxon to Lonchodraco.
facts.quote: In the analyses, they recovered Ikrandraco as a member of the family Lonchodraconidae, and the sister taxon of Lonchodraco.

facts.statement: Ikrandraco lived during the Aptian stage, between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is debated whether the genus Lonchodectes is valid, as Rodrigues and Kellner (2013) argued it was a nomen dubium and reassigned its species to Lonchodraco.
facts.quote: In 2013, paleontologists Taissa Rodrigues and Alexander Kellner made an extensive review of the species of Ornithocheirus, and stated that the generic name Lonchodectes would have been a nomen dubium, and therefore reassigned both Lonchodectes machaerorhynchus and L. microdon into the genus Lonchodraco, creating Lonchodraco machaerorhynchus and L. microdon.
